data.hypothesis: A factor-two target mapping with 256 threads per block (512 outputs per block) reuses each streamed source across two force accumulators while testing a larger CTA than the previously measured 128-thread factor-two setup. Fewer per-thread accumulators than the selected factor-four parent may reduce register demand, but register use, occupancy, correctness, and timing require controller evaluation; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: This N-body target-axis coarsening path; use the observations as launch-configuration evidence, not a universal factor-size rule.
memory_lessons.claim: Observed valid factor-two variants at 64 and 128 threads measured about 0.002617 s, factor three measured about 0.003500 s, and factor four about 0.004442 s; baseline measured about 0.001847 s. These observations do not establish the cause, but motivate testing a factor-two configuration without assuming it beats baseline.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this factor-two, 256-thread/512-output configuration with full correctness and official timing; inspect compiler register and occupancy diagnostics if available.

data.notes: The launch covers arbitrary N via per-target bounds checks and leaves shared-memory staging disabled. Prior observations provide timing but no register-count or occupancy measurements; this candidate must be assessed with the official correctness suite and timing, plus compiler diagnostics if available.
transformations: Assign two target particles per thread at indices separated by blockDim.x, using separate force accumulators and reusing each source position and mass across both targets.
Set the launch to 256 threads and 512 logical outputs per block with zero shared-memory allocation.
Bounds-check each target independently, skip its self-interaction, and write every valid target once, including partial final tiles for arbitrary N.
